extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of aesthetics, artists, critics, and general readers interested in theories of art and beauty
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and compare historical and philosophical criteria for what counts as beauty or art, as presented in a survey of aesthetic theories. Useful for forming evaluative standards or critiques of artistic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Père André — three kinds of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three kinds of beauty—divine beauty, natural beauty, and artificial beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification of beauty into distinct categories (divine, natural, artificial) as a basis for discussing or judging works of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Batteux / Diderot — art as imitation of nature; aim enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: Art consists in imitating the beauty of nature, its aim being enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard: fidelity to nature and capacity to produce enjoyment are marks of art; this view underlies many 18th-century judgments of artistic merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste decides beauty (French & English view)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is taste that decides what is beautiful; the laws of taste are not laid down and cannot be settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion is subjective and community-based: beauty is determined by taste rather than fixed rules, implying variability and lack of definitive standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pagano — art unites dispersed beauties (taste + genius)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art consists in uniting the beauties dispersed in nature. The capacity to perceive these beauties is taste; the capacity to bring them into one whole is artistic genius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes the artist's synthetic power to gather and integrate disparate natural beauties into a coherent whole; moral goodness is linked to beauty in this view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muratori / Spaletti — art as egotistical sensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Art amounts to an egotistical sensation, founded on the desire for self-preservation and society (similar to Burke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats aesthetic response as rooted in biological/self-interested drives; judges art by how it satisfies such impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hemsterhuis — beauty gives most pleasure via many ideas quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is that which gives most pleasure, and that gives most pleasure which gives us the greatest number of ideas in the shortest time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative emphasis on cognitive richness and density: works provoking many ideas rapidly are considered most beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kant — beauty as disinterested pleasure; aesthetic judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty in its subjective meaning is that which, necessarily, without reasonings and without practical advantage, pleases. Objectively, it is the form perceived without conception of utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: 'disinterested' pleasure and lack of practical purpose; art judged by form that pleases independently of utility or desire (Urteilskraft).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schiller — art as play; beauty as disinterested pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of art is beauty, the source of which is pleasure without practical advantage; art may be called a game — a manifestation of life's beauties without other aim than beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard: art's value lies in disinterested play and aesthetic pleasure rather than utility or moral instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wilhelm Humboldt — exposition of various forms of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains various forms of beauty (drama, music, comic, etc.) without changing definition of beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation recognizes genre-specific manifestations; judges should consider how different arts instantiate the shared notion of beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fichte — beauty depends on observer's point of view; art educates whole man
rubrics_metrics.description: The world has two sides (limitations and free idealistic activity); deformity or beauty depends on the point of view of the observer. Art is the manifestation of a beautiful soul and aims at educating the whole man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: aesthetic value rooted in subjective perspective and moral/spiritual education; art assessed by its capacity to manifest an inner 'beautiful soul' and educate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friedrich Schlegel — beauty as union of art, nature and love
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty exists not only in art but also in nature and in love; the truly beautiful is expressed by the union of art, nature, and love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative emphasis on synthesis and holistic unity across domains; good art integrates multiple spheres of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adam Müller — two kinds of beauty (general and individual); harmony reconciles contradictions
rubrics_metrics.description: One kind, general beauty (found chiefly in antique art), the other, individual beauty (modern art). Highest beauty harmonises contradictions; every work of art reproduces universal harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art judged by its relation to universal harmony or by its capacity to create an attracting individuality; high merit when contradictions are reconciled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schelling — beauty as perception of the infinite in the finite; art as knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the production of the conception by which the subject becomes its own object; beauty is the perception of the infinite in the finite; unconscious infinity is characteristic of works of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on art's metaphysical capacity to reveal the infinite within finite forms; art valued as a mode of knowledge and revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solger — idea of beauty is fundamental; art akin to creation
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of beauty is the fundamental idea of everything; art, by imagination, may lift itself to the height of this idea and is akin to creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: proximity to the fundamental idea of beauty and creative imagination that elevates material to the ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krause — beauty as manifestation of the Idea in individual form; art actualises spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: True beauty is the manifestation of the Idea in an individual form; art is the actualisation of beauty in the sphere of man's free spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art by its success in embodying universal Ideas within individual, spiritual forms; highest art adorns life itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hegel — beauty as the Idea shining through matter; art as sensuous manifestation of spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is the shining of the Idea through matter. Art is the production of the appearance of the Idea; the sensuous manifestation of spirit is appearance and is the reality of the beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard: art's worth measured by how effectively it makes spiritual Ideas sensuously manifest; art, religion, and philosophy are means to express deepest human truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weisse / Ruge / Vischer — variations on Idea-as-beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Weisse: introduction of absolute spiritual beauty into matter; Ruge: beauty is the Idea expressing itself; Vischer: beauty is the Idea in finite phenomenon and higher ideas contain more beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate according to the degree and clarity with which works embody or express the Idea/spiritual content; higher subject-matter (personality) yields higher art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Herbart — beauty as relations among impressions; art finds relations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no beauty existing in itself; bases of opinion are connected with impressions. There are certain relations we term beautiful; art consists in finding these relations (simultaneous or successive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative focus on formal relations among elements (lines, colours, succession) rather than metaphysical content; technical relations in art are decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schopenhauer — beauty via renunciation of individuality; genius perceives objectified Will
rubrics_metrics.description: Renunciation of one's individuality and contemplation of planes of manifestation of Will gives perception of beauty; genius has higher capacity to objectivize the Idea and make higher beauty manifest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art assessed by capacity to transcend individual desires and reveal higher manifestations of Will; genius is measured by depth of contemplation and objectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hartmann — beauty lies in the 'seeming' produced by the artist
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty lies not in the thing in itself but in the 'seeming' produced by the artist; the thing in itself is transformed into beauty by the artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: artist's transformative power to produce an appearance that confers beauty; emphasis on artistic mediation rather than inherent object qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schnasse — art supplies what nature cannot; beauty disclosed in free ego
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no perfect beauty in the world; art gives what nature cannot give. Beauty is disclosed in the energy of the free ego conscious of harmony not found in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art by its imaginative or creative additions beyond nature and the expression of a conscious, harmonising ego.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kirkmann — experimental/relational realms of history; art as activity in beauty realm
rubrics_metrics.description: History comprises realms (Knowledge, Wealth, Morality, Faith, Politics, Beauty); activity in beauty is art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework for situating art within cultural-historical functions; assess art by its role and activity within the 'realm of Beauty'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helmholtz (on music) — beauty follows unalterable laws; often unconscious
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty in musical productions is attained only by following unalterable laws. These laws are not known to the artist; beauty is manifested unconsciously and cannot be subjected to analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate musical art against objective, perhaps scientific, laws of perception—even if artists are unaware; suggests formal constraints determine beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bergmann — beauty cannot be defined objectively; perceived subjectively
rubrics_metrics.description: To define beauty objectively is impossible. Beauty is only perceived subjectively, and therefore the problem is to define 'what pleases whom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation becomes empirical/psychological: focus on audiences and subjective reception rather than universal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jungmann — beauty as suprasensible quality producing contemplative pleasure and foundation of love
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is a suprasensible quality of things; it produces in us pleasure by mere contemplation and is the foundation of love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess art for its capacity to evoke contemplative pleasure and to ground emotional bonds like love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cousin — beauty has a moral foundation; variety in unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty always has a moral foundation; it may be defined objectively and essentially consists in variety in unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: moral content and formal unity amid variety; judge works by moral resonance and coherent complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jouffroy — beauty as expression of the invisible through natural signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is the expression of the invisible by those natural signs which manifest it; the visible world is the garment by means of which we see beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on symbolic expressiveness: how well a work uses visible forms to convey invisible truths or states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictet / Lévêque / Ravaisson — idealist/metaphysical beauty (divine/manifestation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty exists in the free manifestation of the divine Idea (Pictet); beauty as invisible force or spirit revealing itself in ordered energy (Lévêque); beauty as ultimate aim/purpose of the world (Ravaisson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess art for its metaphysical consonance with divine or cosmic order; emphasis on spiritual or teleological justification of beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renouvier — truth should be beautiful; beauty conflated with truth
rubrics_metrics.description: A truth which would not be beautiful would be only a logical play; the only solid truth is beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion conflates epistemic and aesthetic value: judge art by its perceived truthfulness insofar as it is beautiful; a controversial metaphysical stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taine — beauty as manifestation of essential characteristic of an idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is the manifestation of the essential characteristic of any important idea more completely than it is expressed in reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes fidelity to and amplification of central ideas; works judged by how fully they embody an idea's essence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guyau — beauty as blossoming of what it appears on; art lifts to universal life
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is not exterior to the object but is the blossoming forth of that on which it appears. Art expresses reasonable and conscious life, evoking deep consciousness and loftiest thoughts; it lifts man from personal life into universal life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess art by its capacity to reveal inner potentialities and to elevate individual experience toward universal significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cherbuliez — art satisfies love of forms, endows them with ideas, and affords pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is an activity satisfying our innate love of forms, endowing these forms with ideas, affording pleasure to senses, heart, and reason. Beauty is an act of our souls; there is no absolute beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-dimensional criterion: formal appeal + intellectual content + affective pleasure; beauty is subjective and acts of the soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coster — innate ideas of beautiful, good, true; unity, variety, order
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas of the beautiful, the good, and the true are innate and identical with God. The idea of Beauty includes unity of essence, variety of elements, and order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art for alignment with innate ideals, unity-with-diversity, and ordered composition; presupposes a transcendent standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Véron — art as manifestation of emotion via external combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the manifestation of emotion transmitted externally by a combination of lines, forms, colours, or by a succession of movements, sounds, or words subjected to certain rhythms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: effective external transmission of emotion through formal means and rhythm; judge by emotional clarity and formal means of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Darwin — beauty as biologically rooted; shared with animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is a feeling natural to man and animals; birds adorn nests and esteem beauty in mates. Origin of music in male call to females.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art with attention to evolutionary/biological origins and functions (sexual selection, signalling), considering cross-species continuities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Herbert Spencer — origin of art is play; sources of aesthetic pleasure threefold
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin of art is play; aesthetic pleasures arise from (1) exercise of faculties with few drawbacks, (2) difference of stimulus in large amount, (3) partial revival with special combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess art by how it engages faculties, provides optimal stimulation, and evokes echoes of previous experiences in novel combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Todhunter — beauty apprehended by reason and enthusiasm of love; recognition depends on taste/culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is infinite loveliness apprehended by reason and enthusiasm of love. Recognition of beauty depends on taste, with the only approach to definition found in culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation depends on cultural training and taste; art's merit judged by capacity to inspire rational appreciation and passionate love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Allen — physiological aesthetics; beauty has physical origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty has a physical origin; aesthetic pleasures come from physiological processes. Origin of art is play and surplus power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge art partly by physiological effects and how it stimulates sensory/neurological responses; taste can be educated by conditioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ker — beauty unites one and many; art makes objective world intelligible without reference to other parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty enables us to make part of the objective world intelligible without reference to other parts; art destroys opposition between one and many, law and manifestation, subject and object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art for capacity to synthesize and render aspects of reality intelligible in themselves; emphasis on unifying power of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knight — beauty as union of object and subject; drawing forth cognate in nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty is the union of object and subject, drawing forth from nature what is cognate to man and recognition in oneself of what is common to all nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: art succeeds when it elicits recognition of shared qualities between subject and object; empathic resonance is central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sully — art as production supplying active enjoyment to producer and pleasure to spectators
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the production of some permanent object or passing action fitted to supply active enjoyment to the producer and a pleasurable impression to spectators or listeners, apart from personal advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical criterion: art judged by producer's enjoyment and the public pleasure it yields; de-emphasises metaphysical beauty and focuses on experiential outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: General critique — beauty-as-pleasure (subjective) vs. beauty-as-objective (mystical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two fundamental conceptions emerge: (1) beauty as something having an independent existence (Idea, Spirit, God), (2) beauty as a kind of pleasure received by us not having personal advantage. Both reduce to the reception of a certain kind of pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-criterion: recognize that many historic standards ultimately equate to subjective pleasure; evaluators should be aware of this convergence and its limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of defining art by beauty/taste/canon
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing aesthetics often define art by what pleases or by an art canon drawn from works already accepted as 'great' (Phidias, Shakespeare, Beethoven, etc.); this method is circular and insufficient for a true definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept as legitimate a standard that retrofits theory to a preselected canon. Avoid circular reasoning: first define art by independent criteria, then judge works by that definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of basing art's aim on pleasure (analogy with food)
rubrics_metrics.description: To see the aim and purpose of art in the pleasure we get from it is mistaken—like asserting the purpose of food is merely the pleasure of eating; the true meaning of an activity must be understood in its causes and effects, not merely its pleasurable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative practice should look beyond pleasurable effects to the activity's functions, relations, causes, and consequences; avoid equating superficial pleasure with artistic purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological requirement — define activity by its sense, causes, and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: To define any human activity (including art) it is necessary to examine it in itself, in dependence on its causes, and in connection with its effects, not merely in relation to the pleasure it produces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed evaluative method: ground definitions and judgments of art in analysis of purpose, causes, and social/psychological consequences rather than in subjective taste alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning against expanding standards to include new works without judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: When novel or debased productions gain acceptance, critics may widen standards to include them rather than judge them by prior standards (example: Muther accommodating Pre-Raphaelites and Symbolists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain critical independence: resist adjusting core evaluative standards merely to accommodate fashions or newly accepted works; evaluate innovations by consistent principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of 'no demand for morality' argument based on canon inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Folgeldt argues we must not demand morality in art because canonical works with immoral content would be excluded; Tolstoy rejects using canon membership as proof against moral demands in art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use canon membership to excuse absence of moral considerations; moral criteria for art must be judged on independent grounds, not by appeal to tradition.
